partners.mechanism_chain: Dominant SLC4A1 mutations (e.g., South East Asian ovalocytosis mutations) (PMID:21771077) —DISRUPTS→ SLC4A1 (HGNC:10676); SLC4A1 (HGNC:10676) —DISRUPTS→ Erythrocyte membrane integrity and function (GO:0030010); Erythrocyte membrane integrity and function (GO:0030010) —LEADS_TO→ Southeast Asian ovalocytosis (HP:0001881); Hemoglobin variants (e.g., unstable hemoglobin) (PMID:24685998) —DISRUPTS→ HBA1/HBA2/HBB (HGNC:4827,HGNC:4828,HGNC:1072); HBA1/HBA2/HBB (HGNC:4827,HGNC:4828,HGNC:1072) —PRODUCES→ Oxidized hemoglobin (CHEBI:61642); Oxidized hemoglobin (CHEBI:61642) —DISRUPTS→ Erythrocyte membrane integrity and function (GO:0030010); Erythrocyte membrane integrity and function (GO:0030010) —LEADS_TO→ Heinz body anemia (HP:0001880). Mutations in SLC4A1 (band 3 protein) in southeast Asian ovalocytosis disrupt erythrocyte membrane integrity, leading to characteristic oval-shaped red blood cells. Concurrently, mutations in hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB) can lead to unstable or oxidizable hemoglobin, which upon oxidation forms Heinz bodies. Both oxidized hemoglobin and altered band 3 protein can compromise erythrocyte membrane integrity and function, ultimately contributing to anemia. The shared convergence point is the disruption of erythrocyte membrane integrity and function, impacting red blood cell survival and leading to distinct but related anemias.
